result.topic_en: A list of research notes: upper bounds for the coefficients of the characteristic function following Noether, representations of a multiple of a ternary form as a sum of three squares, counting contact curves via Abelian functions, and finiteness of integral invariants of an integral linear substitution.

items.english: Seek, according to Noether's principles (large prize paper in Crelle vol. 93), in general the upper bounds for the coefficients of the characteristic function when the first coefficient (order n) and the degree (the dimension δ) are given.

items.english: If f is a given ternary form, for which forms (multipliers) M is then Mf = φ² + ψ² + χ²?

items.english: How many such representations are there? (Generalization of Sylvester's law of inertia, and the same for quaternary etc. forms.)

items.english: Problem: Proof that, when a linear substitution with integer coefficients is given, it has only a finite number of invariants (i.e. integral integer-coefficient functions of the n variables) by which all other integral integer-coefficient invariants can be expressed integrally and with integer coefficients.
